answer: A recurrent net must step through positions one by one because it generates a sequence of hidden states where each state depends on the previous hidden state and the current input, creating an inherently sequential nature that precludes parallelization within training examples [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 2, §1 Introduction]. As the sequence gets longer, the number of sequential operations required increases linearly (O(n)), and the maximum path length between any two input and output positions also increases (O(n)), which makes learning long-range dependencies more difficult [Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 6, §4 Why Self-Attention][Attention Is All You Need, arXiv:1706.03762v7, PDF p. 6].
question: Inside a single training example, why does a recurrent net have to step through positions one by one, and what gets worse as the sequence gets longer?
